column2: Their holy place was named by that name in the three worlds, the Vyasa-tirtha, supreme, which washes the mud of sin, removes the darkness and intoxication of delusion, and grants men all success.

And Kadru likewise; I went with her, and a dispute arose between me and Kadru; I was defeated by her through a trick.
brahmapuran:159:10	Fate is mighty, dear one; what effort does it not make? Thus I became a slave to Kadru, son of Kashyapa; and when I became a slave, you, twice-born, became a slave too.
Then Garuda became silent, exceedingly distressed; he said nothing to his mother, reflecting on what was bound to be.
Once Kadru, wishing the good of her sons and wishing her own prosperity, said to Vinata, mother of the bird:
Your son goes unhindered to bow to the Sun; ah, you are blessed in these three worlds even as a slave.
Hiding her own sorrow, she, very astonished, said to Kadru:
Why do your sons not go to see the Sun?
Take my sons, fortunate one, to the abode of the Nagas; near the ocean there is a cool lake.
Suparna carried the Nagas, and Kadru and Vinata; then she, glad, said to the mother of Vainateya (Garuda):
Garuda is to take my sons to the abode of the gods; again the mother of serpents said to the modest Garuda:
My sons wish to see the Swan, teacher of the three worlds; after bowing to the Sun they will come to my abode. You, take my sons daily to the Sun's disc.
Trembling, the wretched Vinata said to Kadru:
I am not able, mother of serpents; my son will not take them. Let your sons, after seeing the day-making god, go back.
Vinata said to her son, lord of birds: "The Nagas, having come to lordship, wish to bow down."
The mother of serpents said to me by force, 'to the Sun.' Saying "So be it," Garuda said, "Let the serpents mount me."
Then, with the serpent host mounted, the lord of birds Garuda slowly went to where the god, the Day-maker, was; burning in the Sun's sharp heat they writhed.
Turn back, greatly wise one! Salutations to the Sun again and again! Enough of the Sun's abode; we are burnt by the Sun's heat; either you or we should go, leaving you.
Thus addressed by the Nagas, he said, "I shall show you the Sun," and quickly went into the sky, facing the Sun.
With their bodies burnt, they fell on that island Viranna in great numbers, hundreds of thousands, tormented, their bodies scorched.
Hearing the distressed cry of her sons fallen on the ground, Kadru, greatly agitated, came to console them.
Kadru said to Vinata: "Your son did a very wicked deed, very dull-witted, for whom there is no peace.
The lord of serpents cannot do otherwise than his master's word; if the great-brilliant Kashyapa were here, there might be a cure.
Otherwise, how can there be peace for my sons, fair one?" Hearing Kadru's words, Vinata, greatly afraid,
said to her great-souled son Garuda, the lord of birds:

This is not the better ornament, son; it is said that it is fitting to behave with modesty, and the opposite is not fitting.
brahmapuran:159:34	Even toward enemies the good should never do crooked things; the moon shines equally on a Vedic scholar and an outcaste.
brahmapuran:159:35	Those men, my son, do harm by tricks who are unable to do it directly by force; they are the lowest of men.
Then Vinata said to that Kadru, mother of serpents:
By what is peace attained for your sons? I shall do it. They have been seized by old age; say how peace can be made.
Kadru then said to Vinata: "The water in Rasatala; by being sprinkled with it, my sons will find peace."
Hearing Kadru's words, in a moment he brought the water from Rasatala and sprinkled those Nagas. Then Garuda said to Maghavan Shatakratu:
And let the clouds rain here, benefactors of the three worlds.
Parjanya thus rained, and welfare came to the Nagas; the Ganga water born in Rasatala is the reviver of Nagas,
which Garuda brought to destroy old age and grief; where the Nagas were sprinkled, that is called Nagalaya.
Because Garuda brought that water from Rasatala, that Ganga water destroys all sins of all.
Because it warded off old age and brought welfare to the Nagas, because the Ganga water born in Rasatala revives the Nagas,
for destroying old age and grief, on the south bank of the Ganga, the river Vanjara came into being, directly bearing nectar.
It removes old age, poverty and torment, and keeps off affliction; the Ganga born in Rasatala and that born in the human world —
their confluence, what more can be described of it, by mere remembrance of which heaps of sins go to destruction?
Who can tell the fruit of bathing and giving there? The wise say there are one hundred and twenty-five thousand holy places there.
Of holy places that give all prosperity and remove all floods of sin, none anywhere equals the Vanjara confluence, by mere remembrance of which calamities perish.
All those Danavas in battle in the southern direction made a great effort, stationed at the southern ocean.
Trikuta, the best of mountains, was formerly the city of the Rakshasas; through its forest all went with them to the southern ocean.
Where all assemble is Mount Malaya; and that region of Malaya then became that of the gods' enemies.
There on the Gautami's bank Shiva is present for the gods; thus the meeting of the gods took place.
The gods, mounted on their own chariots, assembled here and there on the pure sand of the river-mother Gautami.
She who grants desired boons to all the ancestors when pleased — then all the groups of gods, having praised the god Maheshvara, thought of safety among themselves:
What is the means here for us, forcibly defeated by the enemy? One thing alone is best for us: victory or death. Life for the proud overcome by enemies is shameful.
In the meantime, son, a bodiless voice spoke:

Enough of trouble, hosts of gods; go quickly to the Gautami and there worship Hari and Hara, the Lords, with devotion.
brahmapuran:160:19	By the grace of the Godavari and of those two, what is hard to do?
With Hari and Isha pleased, the gods obtained the desired victory and went everywhere, protecting the dwellers in heaven.
Where the gods came, that holy place is famed by that; the sages who see truth praise Devagama.
There, Narada, are eighty thousand Shiva-lingas; the mountain Devagama is also called Priya (dear); from then on they know the holy place as Devapriya.

I shall tell what is more secret than the secret, auspicious, directly declared by the Vedas, which neither sages nor gods, ancestors or Asuras know.
brahmapuran:161:6	I shall tell it for your pleasure; by hearing it all desires are granted. The Supreme Purusha is to be known as the unmanifest, imperishable;
brahmapuran:161:7	and another, perishable, joined with Prakriti, from the formless a Purusha with parts was born.
brahmapuran:161:8	From him the waters arose, and from the waters a Purusha too; from the two a lotus arose, and in it I was born, sage.
brahmapuran:161:9	Earth, wind, space, water and light: these, earlier than me, came to be at once, sage.
brahmapuran:161:10	I see only these, nothing else moving or unmoving; the Vedas were not then, and I could not see anything.
brahmapuran:161:11	Since I was born, I could not see even him; when I stood silent I then heard a supreme voice:
brahmapuran:161:12	'Brahma, create the world of the unmoving and the moving.'
brahmapuran:161:13	Then I spoke a harsh word there, Narada: 'How shall I create, where shall I create, by what shall I create this world?'
brahmapuran:161:14	That same divine voice, which is called Prakriti, sent by Vishnu, the mother, ruler of the world, consisting of the world, said:
brahmapuran:161:15	'Perform a sacrifice; then you will have the power, no doubt. Sacrifice is Vishnu, this is the eternal Shruti, Brahma.
brahmapuran:161:16	What is unattainable for sacrificers here in this world and the next?'
brahmapuran:161:17	Again I said to that goddess, 'Where, and by what? Tell me.' 'A sacrifice must be done, fortunate one.' Then she said to me:
brahmapuran:161:18	'The goddess who is the form of Om, like a mother, consisting of the world: perform sacrifice in the land of action to the Lord of sacrifice, the Sacrifice-Person.
brahmapuran:161:19	He himself will be your instrument; sacrifice to him, good vow-holder. Sacrifice, svaha, svadha, mantras, Brahmins, oblation and the rest —
brahmapuran:161:20	Hari is all that; by him everything of Vishnu is attained.'
brahmapuran:161:21	Again I said to that goddess, 'Where is the land of action established?' Then, Narada, there was neither Bhagirathi nor Narmada,
brahmapuran:161:22	nor Yamuna, nor Tapi, Sarasvati or Gautami, no ocean or great river, no lake, no pure streams. That power again and again said to me:
brahmapuran:161:23	'South of Sumeru, south of the Himalaya mountain, and south of Vindhya, and south of Sahya — for all, at all times, the land of action brings auspicious prosperity.'
brahmapuran:161:24	Hearing that speech, I left the great mountain Meru and, coming to that region, thought: 'Where should I stay?' Then that bodiless voice of Vishnu said to me:
brahmapuran:161:25	'Go from here, stay here, sit here, and make the resolve of the sacrifice; your sacrifice will be completed.'
brahmapuran:161:26	And when the resolve for the sacrifice was made, best of gods, whatever all the Vedas state, do that, Creator.
brahmapuran:161:27	Histories, Puranas and whatever else belongs to the sphere of sound came by itself into my mouth and into the sphere of memory.
brahmapuran:161:28	In that moment I knew the whole meaning of the Vedas, and then I recalled the Purusha Sukta, famed in the world.
brahmapuran:161:29	I arranged, as said, all the requisites of sacrifice; in the manner stated in it I arranged the sacrificial vessels.
brahmapuran:161:30	The region where I stood, pure, self-controlled, and was initiated is the Brahmin region, and it is known by my name.
brahmapuran:161:31	My holy place of sacrifice is called Brahmagiri, extending eighty-four yojanas, great sage.
brahmapuran:161:32	My holy sacrificial ground lies east of Brahmagiri; there in the middle is the altar, and the Garhapatya fire to its south.
brahmapuran:161:33	There I arranged the Ahavaniya and so the fires. A sacrifice is not accomplished without a wife, by the testimony of Shruti.
brahmapuran:161:34	I divided my own body in two, sage; with the first half my wife came into being for the accomplishment of the sacrifice.
brahmapuran:161:35	With the other half I remained so; as Shruti says half is the wife." Spring, the best season, in the form of ghee, Narada,
I arranged; likewise firewood as summer, and autumn as the oblation; the rainy season, son, I then arranged as the sacred grass.
The seven metres became the boundary sticks there; the moments, kashthas and winks were remembered as the fuel-sticks, vessels and kusha.
He who is without beginning and endless, Time himself, then became, sage of the gods, the sacrificial post, and the tie for binding the victim.
The three qualities beginning with sattva were the ropes, but there was no victim there. Then I spoke to the bodiless voice of Vishnu:
'Without a victim this sacrifice will not be completed.' Then that same eternal bodiless goddess said to me:
'Praise the Supreme Purusha with the Purusha Sukta.'
Saying "So be it," I praised the god of gods Janardana, my own originator, with devotion, with the Sukta of the Purusha.
And that goddess said to me, 'Brahma, make me the victim.' Then, knowing the Purusha, my imperishable father,
bound with the ropes of qualities at the side of the post of Time, I sprinkled the Purusha who was seated on the sacred grass, born before.
In the meantime all this arose from him: Brahmins from his mouth, Kshatriyas from his arms,
from his mouth Indra and Agni, from his breath the wind, the quarters from his ear, and from his head all heaven then came.
From his mind the Moon was born, and the Sun from his eye, the atmosphere from his navel, and Vaishyas from his thighs;
from his feet the Shudra was born, and so the Earth; sages from his hair-pores, herbs from his hair.
Village and forest animals came from his nails everywhere; worms, insects, moths and the like were born from the organs of excretion and generation.
Whatever is moving or unmoving, whatever is seen or unseen, all came from him; the gods came and were born again from me. In the meantime that same voice of Vishnu said to me:
'All has become complete, creation has been made as desired. Now offer into the fire, and the vessels equally.
Release the post, the praṇītā water and the kusha; the form of the priests, the form of the sacrifice, the object and the meditation,
the ladle, the Purusha, the ropes — release all, Brahma.'
At the very time of her words, in order, in the womb-fires of the sacrifice, in the Garhapatya, the Dakshina fire, great sage,
and likewise in the eastern fire, offering in order, in each fire, contemplating the Purusha as the world's source,
purified by mantras, the pure sacrificial god, the world-consisting Lord of the world, universal maker, present at the fire-pits there —
Vishnu is white in the Ahavaniya; Vishnu is dark in the Dakshina fire; Vishnu is yellow in the Garhapatya, the Kavi.
Vishnu is at all times in those regions; nothing is without him, Vishnu the womb of the universe.
I performed the leading forth of the Pranita water with mantras; that Pranita water is also the auspicious river called Pranita.
I released that Pranita after cleansing with kusha; and while the cleansing was done, drops of Pranita water
fell there and holy places of merit arose; they arose, tiger among sages, giving the fruit of sacrifices by bathing.
The one always adorned by the god of gods, Sharngin (Vishnu), that row of steps ascends to Vaikuntha for all.
Where the cleansed kusha fell on the auspicious ground, Kushatarpana is declared, giving the fruit of much merit.
All were satisfied by kusha; it is called Kushatarpana. Afterwards the Gautami joined there for another reason,
greatly wise one: the confluence with Pranita occurred, and at the Kushatarpana region that tirtha is Kushatarpana.
There the post arranged by me, north of Vindhya, was released; worshipped by the world, it became Vishnu's support.
The glorious one became imperishable; that banyan became Akshaya, eternal, of the form of Time; by mere remembrance it gives the merit of a sacrifice.
This place of sacrifice of mine is called Dandakaranya. When the sacrifice was complete, Vishnu was propitiated by me with devotion,
who is called Virat in the Veda, from whom the embodied came, from whom my origin is, whose is this transformed world.
Having bowed to that Lord of lords I dismissed him; my holy sacrificial ground extends twenty-four yojanas.
Therefore even today there are three fire-pits, Narada, forms of the Lord of sacrifice, of Vishnu, the discus-bearer.
From then on it is called my sacrificial place; even a worm or insect staying there becomes in the end a recipient of liberation.
Dandakaranya is called the seed of dharma and the seed of liberation; especially, being joined with the Gautami, the region became most holy.
One who does bathing, giving and the like at the Pranita confluence or at Kushatarpana reaches the supreme state.
Remembrance, reciting or hearing with devotion, they know, grants men all desires, enjoyment and liberation.
On both banks there, the wise say, are holy places; eighty-six thousand, and the merit in them was told earlier.
Even more than Varanasi, sage, Kushatarpana is best; no holy place is equal to this in the world of moving and unmoving.
Even by remembrance it destroys sins such as Brahmin-slaying; this holy place, sage, is told as the door of heaven on earth.
Then the revered Maheshvara, trident in hand, pleased, said to the gods, "Choose what you wish."
The gods said: "For victory give us a man, the lord of the gods, supremely praiseworthy, standing in front in battles,
relying on the strength of whose arms we may be happy." Maheshvara said "So be it" to the gods.
Created by the Supreme Lord from his own brilliance, one named Manyu (Wrath), extremely fierce, leader of the gods' army:
bowing to him, all the gods bowed to Shiva and went to their abodes, and with Manyu came to stand again for battle.
Standing in battle against the Danavas and mighty Daityas, the gods, armoured, standing before Manyu, said:
We see your capability; afterwards we shall fight the enemy. So show yourself, Manyu, to us who wish to fight.
Hearing the gods' word, Manyu said, smiling as it were:

My begetter is the lord of gods, omniscient, all-seeing, who knows everyone's inner abode, name and mind.
brahmapuran:162:17	No one knows him, who knows all always; formless and formed, this all the maker, consisting of the world, knows.
brahmapuran:162:18	He, the revered Supreme, directly, moves in the sky and heaven; who knows his form? Whose maker is he who consists of the world?
brahmapuran:162:19	Born of such a one, how can you know me? Or, if you wish to see, look at me.
Having said so, Manyu showed his own great form, arisen from the third eye of Bhava, the Supreme Lord.
The form, gathered of brilliance, from which all is said, is manliness in men and egoism in creatures.
Anger, terrible in all, that becomes the destroyer, they saw in the representative of Shankara, blazing with his own brilliance,
bearing all weapons; all the deities bowed. The Daityas and Danavas were frightened; the gods, with joined palms,
said to Manyu: "Lord, be our general; this kingdom given by you, Manyu, we shall enjoy.
Therefore in all tasks you are the conqueror, increaser of victory; you are Indra, you Varuna, and you the world-guardians.
Enter into us, all the gods, for victory." Manyu said to them all: "Without me there is nothing.
I have entered all within; no one knows me. That same Manyu, the Lord, was born from him separately, each differently.
He alone is of Rudra's form; Rudra, Manyu, became Shiva. Everything unmoving and moving is pervaded by Manyu."
